questions.prompt: A car at 50 km/h travels about 14 m in the 1 second a driver takes to react. Explain why lower speed limits near schools make children safer.
questions.modelAnswer: At lower speeds, the car travels a shorter distance during the driver's reaction time and while braking, so it can stop sooner. This gives children more chance to be safe if they step onto the road, and a crash at lower speed causes less injury.
rubric: Lower speed → shorter distance travelled while reacting/braking
The car can stop sooner / before hitting someone
Less injury if a collision happens
questions.explain: Physics helps us make evidence-based safety decisions (Criterion D).
